text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to $135.51, continuing a sharp 7% decline over the past two weeks. The immediate trigger was the company's quarterly earnings announcement on November 5th, but the bigger picture is the collapse in oil prices—crude has tumbled from $150 at the end of October to under $100 per barrel today, cutting directly into the revenue an oil producer like ConocoPhillips can generate.

The broader headwind is political uncertainty. Democrats' recent midterm success means incoming scrutiny of energy deals and Venezuela policy, which creates regulatory risk for major oil companies. Combined with weakening global oil demand signals, investors are rotating away from traditional energy stocks and toward renewables, putting steady pressure on the sector this week.
